Romanian F-16s shoot down two Geran-family drones off Sulina

17 October 2026 · Sulina · Two attack drones shot down over territorial waters

MApN-confirmed shoot-down of two attack drones

Romania’s defence ministry says two F-16s shot down two jet-powered Geran-family attack drones over Romanian territorial waters on 17 October 2026. The first was southeast of Sulina at 18:01 EEST, the second east of Sulina at 18:05.

The ministry reports two and five minutes respectively in national airspace before interception. This is one operation involving two drones; the statement does not identify the operator or intended targets. The map anchor is approximate.

On 18 October, Defence Minister Radu Miruță assessed the drones as likely Russian-origin Geran 4. Exact model and propulsion subtype remain uncertain, and the launch operator and intended targets remain unestablished.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
MApN identified the Geran family. On 18 October, Defence Minister Radu Miruță assessed the drones as likely Russian-origin Geran 4, citing their reported speed of approximately 450 km/h. This is a tentative origin/model assessment, not confirmation of the launch operator or intended targets.
Investigation / uncertainty
Exact model and propulsion subtype remain unresolved: MApN calls the drones jet-powered, while the minister's later remarks use turbo-propulsor, rendered as turboprop by Reuters. His Geran 4 identification is tentative. Launch operator, intended targets and precise coordinates remain unpublished.
